Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Scaffold generator: opt-in write gating and an explicit game-path migration flag

## Goal

As the engine maintainer, I want `game-repo-scaffold.ts` to stop overwriting
consumer-owned wiring by default and to stop applying the
`example-games/<game>/` → `src/` codemod to every file on every run, so a
re-scaffold of the live `tce-main-street` checkout can no longer silently gut
its build/test wiring.

Created from `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` (producer decision Q2=A). That item's
acceptance criteria are carried over here in full; the `MS` item is closed once
this item exists.

## Producer decisions (2026-10-31)

- **Q1 = B — explicit selection, not a changed default.** Keep today's
  behaviour for fresh/extracted game repos; add `--only <file,...>`, `--force`
  and `--dry-run`; the main-street `scaffold` script opts in to `main.ts` only.
- **Q2 = A — this item owns the generator change**, test-first in the engine
  repo, followed by an engine pin bump in `tce-main-street`.
- **Q3 = A — `rewriteGameTreePaths` becomes opt-in** via
  `--migrate-game-paths` (default off); fresh repos are already renamed by
  `extract-repos.sh --path-rename`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Generator write gating.** `scaffoldGameRepo`/the CLI accept
   `--only <file,...>` (restrict the run to the named generated files; no other
   file, symlink or rewrite is performed), `--force` (allow overwriting a file
   whose content differs from the template) and `--dry-run` (report every file
   as `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`, writing nothing). Default
   behaviour for extracted repos is unchanged: a full scaffold still writes all
   generated files.
2. **Write reporting.** Every run (dry or real) prints a machine-readable
   summary of the classification per file, so a consumer can see what a run
   would touch before trusting it.
3. **Path rewrite is opt-in.** `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` and the
   accompanying quoted-path/alias rewrites run only with
   `--migrate-game-paths`; without it, no file under `tests/` or `src/` is
   modified. `--migrate-game-paths` also reports the files it rewrites.
4. **Engine tests (test-first).** `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
   gains tests written **before** the implementation for: `--only` restricting
   writes, `--dry-run` writing nothing while classifying correct, `--force`
   required to replace a diverged file, default-on-path-rewrite removed
   (no-op without the flag) and preserved with the flag. The full engine suite
   passes.
5. **Main-street consumer wiring.** In the `tce-main-street` checkout:
   `package.json`'s `scaffold` script passes `--only main.ts` (plus the flag
   name chosen in AC1); `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` copies
   this repo's `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`,
   `env.d.ts`, `main.ts` and representative `tests/` files into a temporary
   directory, runs the scaffold against it and fails if any protected wiring
   file changes (while asserting `main.ts` is regenerated);
   `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` replaces the interim "classify-and-revert"
   rule with the new default and opt-in. All related documentation is updated
   (code comments in the generator explain why the overwrite is gated; any
   README or docs-site text describing the scaffold command is corrected).
6. **Stability and validation.** `npm run scaffold` in `tce-main-street` twice in
   a row leaves `git status --porcelain` empty except for opted-in paths; the
   engine pin bump (gitlink + `configs/engine-pin.json` together) is a
   deliberate commit in `tce-main-street`; `npm run build` and the changed-scope
   gate pass there; the full project test suite passes.

## Scope and delivery (two repos)

1. **Engine repo (`Tableau-Card-Engine`, `dev`)** — generator change +
   engine-side tests (AC1–AC4). This is the item's primary worktree.
2. **Consumer repo (`tce-main-street`, `dev`)** — script wiring, regression
   test, docs, engine pin bump (AC5–AC6).

If worktree isolation prevents editing `tce-main-street` from this item's
worktree, create an `MS` follow-up item during planning that carries AC5–AC6
verbatim and link it here; AC5–AC6 must never be dropped.

## Constraints

- **Do not change the default for extracted repos.** The eight sibling repos
  (`tce-golf` etc.) keep the plain `scaffold` invocation and must still receive
  template updates from a full run.
- **Never run the destructive path** against a live checkout while developing;
  experiment in a temp directory or the worktree.
- **Engine pin discipline:** the pin (`configs/engine-pin.json`) and the `core`
  gitlink travel together in one deliberate commit; never a build side effect.
- Repository boundaries: only the generator, its tests, the consumer
  `package.json`/docs/tests and the engine pin are in scope.

## Existing state

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`: `writeFile()` writes unconditionally
  (no content comparison, no dry-run, no allow-list); `parseArgs` supports only
  `--game`, `--game-repo-root`, `--core-root`, `--core-rel`, `--version`,
  `--all`, `--repos-dir`, `--layout`.
- `rewriteGameTreePaths()` walks all of `tests/**` and `src/**` and applies four
  textual rewrites to every `.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs/.js` file whether or not it
  references the game tree.
- `index.html` is copied verbatim from `core/index.html`; `renderPackageJson`
  inherits the core's scripts and dependencies — both clobber local wiring in a
  live checkout.
- One observed run on a clean `dev` tree rewrote 11 files besides `main.ts`,
  including the drift guard's own `STALE_PREFIX`, a run-tests import (`→
  @core-scripts/run-tests`) and 250 lines of documented LOCAL SURGICAL
  ADDITIONS in `vite.config.ts`. Full table on `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB`.

## Key Files

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — write gating (`--only`, `--force`,
  `--dry-run`), classification reporting, `--migrate-game-paths` gating in
  `scaffoldGameRepo` + `parseArgs`, rationale comments.
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — engine-side tests (AC4).
- `tce-main-street/package.json` — scope the `scaffold` script.
- `tce-main-street/tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` — new
  regression guard (temp-copy harness); follow the style of
  `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts`.
- `tce-main-street/docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — document default + opt-in.
- `tce-main-street/configs/engine-pin.json` — pin bump.
- `tce-main-street/main.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html` —
  protected inputs for the regression harness (not to be edited).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `main.ts` is the only file main-street currently wants
  regenerated (per `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH`).
- **Risk:** a cross-repo delivery from one worktree may violate worktree
  isolation — mitigated by the explicit split-and-link rule above.
- **Risk:** `--only` interacting with symlink/asset linking could leave a repo
  half-scaffolded — mitigate by making `--only` skip links entirely and
  reporting that it did.
- **Risk:** temp-copy harness drift — mitigate by copying real repo files rather
  than inlining fixtures.
- **Scope-creep risk:** generator script hygiene (broken `scaffold:game` keys)
  is tracked separately in `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0`; link, do not absorb.

## Related work

- `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` — origin item (intake brief, producer decisions,
  observed damage table). Closed on creation of this item.
- `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH` / `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7` — the re-scaffold that exposed
  the hazard.
- `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0` and children — generator-emitted script hygiene
  (separate scope).
- `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` — template improvement that relies on re-scaffold
  remaining usable.
- `CG-0MVPWPWLA008FTDJ`, `CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA` — precedent template fixes that
  re-scaffold propagates.

## Plan (2026-10-31)

**Decomposition — five child items, test-first inside each slice.** Test-first is satisfied *within* each child (failing tests authored first, then the implementation, then a green build → test → commit cycle); no standalone RED child exists because this repo gates every commit on a green suite, so a tests-only child could not be committed. The children cut vertically through the layers they touch: generator code, generator tests, CLI `--help`, and the rationale/doc prose that belongs to the slice. Consumer prose lives in the engine docs child; the consumer repo work is the MS follow-up.

| # | Child | Slice | Parent ACs |
|---|-------|-------|------------|
| 1 | `CG-0MVWGJNQM0061W6I` Scaffold write classification, dry-run and report | classification pipeline, `--dry-run`, `--json` report, typed `ScaffoldResult.files` | AC1 (`--dry-run`), AC2, AC4 |
| 2 | `CG-0MVWGJPPA000GBE7` Only allow-list, force and skip-local gating | `--only`, `--force`, `skip-local`, side-effect suppression, fail-fast name validation | AC1, AC4 |
| 3 | `CG-0MVWGJRIO0094Y4Z` Gate path rewrite behind migrate-game-paths | `--migrate-game-paths` opt-in, dry-run preview, mutual exclusion with `--only` | AC3, AC4 |
| 4 | `CG-0MVWGJTDL00576GQ` Document scaffold write gating in engine docs | `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, generator header cross-reference | AC5 (docs clause) |
| 5 | `CG-0MVWGJUU3003J7HA` Main-street wiring, guard, docs and pin bump | cross-repo delivery, tracked as `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` (AC5 + AC6 verbatim) | AC5, AC6 |

**Dependency order:** 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 (`wl dep add` edges wired). Child 5 is a tracking/verification child: the code, test, doc and pin-bump work is executed in `tce-main-street` under `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`, because this item's worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-…`) cannot write outside the core checkout — the parent's own scope note requires exactly this split, and AC5–AC6 must not be dropped.

**Recorded design decision (AC1's `--force` interaction).** AC1 lists `--force` and the `skip-local` classification, while the Constraints require a plain full run to keep propagating template updates to the eight sibling repos. The only reading in which both hold — and in which `--force` is not dead code — is:

- **No `--only`** → today's behaviour: every diverged generated file is rewritten (`update`). Implemented as `effectiveForce = force || only === undefined`.
- **With `--only`** → only the named files are candidates; a named file that exists and differs is `skip-local` (untouched) unless `--force` is passed, and every unselected file is `skip-local`. Selection mode suppresses the `core` symlink, shared-asset links, root app-icon links and the game-tree path rewrite entirely.
- `--only` + `--migrate-game-paths` is rejected as a conflict (selection promises "no rewrite").

Consequence: the `tce-main-street` scaffold script becomes `--only main.ts --force` (AC5's "plus the flag name chosen in AC1"). This interpretation is implemented by children 2–3 and consumed by `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`; it is recorded here so the audit can check intent rather than re-derive it.

**Other recorded assumptions**

- `main.ts` is the only file `tce-main-street` wants regenerated (per `MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH`); `configs/game.json` may be opted in later by the same mechanism.
- `--json` is the machine-readable report surface (one document per run: an object for `--game`, an array for `--all`); the classification vocabulary stays exactly `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`.
- The generator's script-hygiene defects (`scaffold:game` keys) stay with `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0` — linked, not absorbed.

**Duplicate check:** `wl search scaffold` / `wl search "scaffold generator write gating"` against the core store returned no non-terminal overlapping item; the closest completed items (`CG-0MVSIB5LH0069LB3`, `CG-0MVPWPWLA008FTDJ`, `CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA`) are template fixes this plan's full-run back-compatibility must keep propagating.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The producer answered the design questions on `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` (2026-10-31) before this item was created; that record is the authoritative source and is not re-asked here.

- Q1: "Should the generator change its default, or expose explicit selection while keeping today's default?" Answer (producer): "**B — explicit selection, not a changed default.** Keep today's behaviour for fresh/extracted game repos; add `--only <file,...>`, `--force` and `--dry-run`; the main-street `scaffold` script opts in to `main.ts` only." Final: B.
- Q2: "Which repo owns the generator change, and does it also own the consumer wiring?" Answer (producer): "**A — this item owns the generator change**, test-first in the engine repo, followed by an engine pin bump in `tce-main-street`." Final: A.
- Q3: "Should `rewriteGameTreePaths` stay on by default?" Answer (producer): "**A — `rewriteGameTreePaths` becomes opt-in** via `--migrate-game-paths` (default off); fresh repos are already renamed by `extract-repos.sh --path-rename`." Final: A.
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Does a selected file that diverges from the template get written unconditionally, or only with `--force`?" Answer (plan, from AC1 + the extracted-repo constraint): only with `--force`; a full run keeps today's unconditional rewrite. Recorded as the "Recorded design decision" above. Evidence: AC1 (`--force` "allow overwriting a file whose content differs from the template"), Constraints ("the eight sibling repos … must still receive template updates from a full run").
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Can `tce-main-street` be edited from this item's worktree?" Answer (plan, from the parent's scope note + worktree isolation): no — create the `MS` follow-up `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` carrying AC5–AC6 verbatim. Final: MS follow-up created.
- Q (planning, resolved without escalation): "Which consumer docs still describe the scaffold command?" Answer (plan, repo inspection): `tce-main-street/docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (re-scaffold references) and `tce-main-street/docs/dev/testing.md` (three passages claiming `npm run scaffold` regenerates the `resolve.dedupe` and transcript-persist wiring). The MS follow-up corrects both; the engine docs child covers `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `README.md`.

**OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for the audit review):** none — the flagged interpretation above is an implementation detail inside the producer's fixed design space, documented rather than escalated.

# Scaffold write classification, `--dry-run` and a machine-readable report

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — engine slice covering AC1 (`--dry-run`), AC2 and the dry-run half of AC4.

## Target outcome

A scaffold run classifies every file it generates **before** touching the disk, returns that classification in its typed result and prints it for every run; `--dry-run` performs the identical classification and writes nothing.

## Behaviour contract

- Generated-file set unchanged: `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `env.d.ts`, `main.ts`, `index.html` (still copied from `core/index.html`) and `configs/game.json`.
- Classification vocabulary is fixed by the parent AC and must keep this shape in later slices: `create` (target absent), `update` (exists and differs from the template → written), `unchanged` (exists, byte-identical), `skip-local` (exists and differs, not written). This slice produces only `create` / `update` / `unchanged`; the `skip-local` discriminator and the `--force` gate that produces it are the next slice.
- `ScaffoldResult` gains `files: ScaffoldFileReport[]` (`{ path, action }`, repo-relative, stable order). The existing `written` array remains as a compatibility projection of the `create` + `update` entries.
- `--dry-run` performs no `mkdirSync`, no `fs.writeFileSync`, no symlink creation, no asset/public link and no path rewrite; `written` / `symlinks` / `assetLinks` / `publicLinks` / `rewritten` come back empty while `files` carries what a real run would do.
- `--json` prints one JSON document for the run (object for a single `--game`, array for `--all`) carrying the same `files` report; human output keeps one line per file (`  create  main.ts`).
- Inline rationale comment in the generator explains **why** writes are classified and gated (a live consumer checkout owns its wiring, so only opted-in files may change) rather than overwritten blindly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC2 carried over verbatim — **Write reporting.** Every run (dry or real) prints a machine-readable summary of the classification per file, so a consumer can see what a run would touch before trusting it. _(covered by this slice (machine-readable per-file report for dry and real runs).)_
- Parent AC4 carried over verbatim — **Engine tests (test-first).** `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` gains tests written **before** the implementation for: `--only` restricting writes, `--dry-run` writing nothing while classifying correct, `--force` required to replace a diverged file, default-on-path-rewrite removed (no-op without the flag) and preserved with the flag. The full engine suite passes. _(this child writes the classification, `--dry-run` and report tests; the sibling children write the `--only`/`--force` and rewrite-opt-in tests, so AC4 closes only when all three engine children are green.)_
- Tests are authored **before** the implementation in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (RED first, then GREEN) covering: an absent file classifies `create` and is created; a byte-identical file classifies `unchanged` and is not rewritten; a diverged file classifies `update` and is overwritten; the `files` report covers every generated file.
- `scaffoldGameRepo({ dryRun: true })` on a temp repo leaves every protected file byte-identical (checksum comparison), creates no `core` symlink, no asset links and performs no path rewrite, while `files` reports the classification the following real run applies.
- A real run's `files` report equals the preceding `--dry-run` report for the same tree (no classification drift between dry and real runs).
- CLI: `--dry-run --json` against a temp repo writes nothing and emits a single parseable JSON document containing a `files` array; `--help` documents `--dry-run` and `--json`.
- The targeted unit run (`/skill:test --type unit` scoped to `tests/scripts/`) and `npm run build` pass; the full engine suite passes at the `dev` push gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace the `writeFile(path, contents, written)` helper with a `classifyAndApply(path, contents, opts)` step returning a `ScaffoldFileReport`, and keep `writeFile` as a thin wrapper so existing call sites stay readable.
- Add `dryRun?: boolean` to `ScaffoldOptions`; thread it through the whole `scaffoldGameRepo` body (file writes, `core` symlink, asset links, public links, path rewrite).
- Export `ScaffoldFileReport` / `ScaffoldFileAction` types; add `files` to `ScaffoldResult`.
- `parseArgs`: `--dry-run`, `--json`; `usage()` entries; `main()` prints the per-file report and the JSON document.
- Tests: extend the existing `scaffoldGameRepo` / `linkShared*` fixtures in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` with a temp-repo harness that pre-seeds generated files, then assert classification, no-write behaviour and dry-vs-real equality.

## Prototype/Experiment

None required — the classification is a byte comparison over a fixed, small file set.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — classification pipeline, `dryRun` option, `files` report, CLI flags, rationale comment.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — new classification/dry-run/report tests (authored first).

## Dependencies

None — this is the first engine slice.

## Deliverables

Typed per-file classification in `ScaffoldResult`, a `--dry-run` mode that writes nothing, a `--json` machine-readable report for both dry and real runs, and green targeted unit + build gates.

# `--only` allow-list, `--force` and `skip-local` write gating

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — engine slice covering the `--only` / `--force` / `skip-local` half of AC1 (and AC4).

## Target outcome

A consumer checkout can opt in to exactly the generated files it wants regenerated. Selecting a subset never touches anything else — no other file, no symlink, no asset link and no path rewrite — and a selected file whose local content differs from the template is only overwritten when the caller explicitly asks for it.

## Behaviour contract

- `ScaffoldOptions.only?: string[]` / CLI `--only <file,...>`. Names are repo-relative generated paths (`main.ts`, `configs/game.json`, `index.html`, …). Selecting a file is the **only** way a run may modify a consumer-owned file.
- Unselected generated files classify `skip-local` and are not written.
- `ScaffoldOptions.force?: boolean` / CLI `--force`. A **selected** file that exists and differs from the template is `skip-local` (not written) unless `--force` is passed, in which case it is `update` (written). Without `--force` the run cannot silently clobber a hand-edited generated file.
- Back-compatibility is preserved exactly: with **no** `--only`, a run behaves as today — every diverged generated file is rewritten — because the eight sibling `tce-<game>` repos rely on a plain full run to receive template updates. Implement this as `effectiveForce = force || only === undefined` and document it in the help text and inline comments (a full run is inherently the "regenerate everything" mode).
- `--only` suppresses all non-file side effects: no `core` symlink creation, no shared-asset links, no root app-icon links, no game-tree path rewrite. The run reports that it skipped them (a one-line note; `symlinks` / `assetLinks` / `publicLinks` / `rewritten` come back empty).
- An unknown name in `--only` fails fast (exit code 1) with a message listing the valid generated paths, and nothing is written — a typo must not produce a silent no-op scaffold.
- Classification reporting from the previous slice is unchanged; `--only` + `--dry-run` reports the same classification the real `--only` run would apply.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1 carried over verbatim — **Generator write gating.** `scaffoldGameRepo`/the CLI accept `--only <file,...>` (restrict the run to the named generated files; no other file, symlink or rewrite is performed), `--force` (allow overwriting a file whose content differs from the template) and `--dry-run` (report every file as `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`, writing nothing). Default behaviour for extracted repos is unchanged: a full scaffold still writes all generated files. _(this slice delivers the `--only`, `--force` and `skip-local` clauses plus the unchanged full-run default.)_
- Tests are authored **before** the implementation in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (RED first, then GREEN) for: `--only main.ts` writing only `main.ts` while every other generated file stays byte-identical and classifies `skip-local`; no `core` symlink / asset link / path rewrite being created in selection mode.
- A diverged selected file stays untouched (`skip-local`) without `--force` and is regenerated (`update`) with `--force`.
- An unknown `--only` name throws / exits 1 with the valid-name list and leaves the temp repo byte-identical.
- A full run (no `--only`) still rewrites a diverged generated file (explicit regression guard for the eight sibling repos), and a full run on an unchanged tree classifies every file `unchanged` and writes nothing.
- `--only main.ts --dry-run` writes nothing and its report matches the following real run's report.
- The targeted unit run (`/skill:test --type unit` scoped to `tests/scripts/`) and `npm run build` pass; the full engine suite passes at the `dev` push gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `only?: string[]` and `force?: boolean` to `ScaffoldOptions`; derive `effectiveForce` and an `isSelected(relPath)` predicate in `scaffoldGameRepo`.
- Route every generated write through the selection predicate; skip the `core` symlink, `linkSharedAssets`, `linkSharedPublicAssets` and `rewriteGameTreePaths` calls when `only` is set, and print the "selection mode" note.
- Validate `--only` names against the generated set up front (before any write) and throw with the sorted valid list; `parseArgs` also enforces that `--only` implies literal names (no globs).
- `parseArgs` / `usage()`: `--only <file,...>` and `--force`, including the note that a full run implies force.
- Tests: extend the classification harness with mismatched-content fixtures and CLI-level assertions (spawn or `parseArgs` + `scaffoldGameRepo` on a temp repo).

## Prototype/Experiment

None required.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `only` / `force` options, selection predicate, side-effect suppression, `skip-local` classification, validation and rationale comments.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — selection/force/`skip-local` tests (authored first).

## Dependencies

- `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` child: _Scaffold write classification, --dry-run and machine-readable report_ — supplies the classification pipeline this slice extends.

## Deliverables

`--only` / `--force` gating with `skip-local` classification, fail-fast validation of selected names, unchanged full-run behaviour for extracted repos, and green targeted unit + build gates.

# Gate the game-tree path rewrite behind `--migrate-game-paths`

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — engine slice covering AC3 (and the opt-in half of AC4).

## Target outcome

`scaffoldGameRepo` no longer rewrites `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` (or the accompanying quoted-path, alias and `scripts/` rewrites) unless the caller explicitly asks for a migration, so a routine re-scaffold can never edit a consumer's tests or source.

## Behaviour contract

- `ScaffoldOptions.migrateGamePaths?: boolean` / CLI `--migrate-game-paths`; **default off**.
- Without the flag `rewriteGameTreePaths()` is not invoked at all: no file under `tests/` or `src/` is modified and `rewritten` is empty. Fresh repos do not need it — `scripts/extract-repos.sh --path-rename` already produced the `src/` layout.
- With the flag the current rewrite behaviour is preserved verbatim (all four textual rewrites) and the affected files are reported both in `ScaffoldResult.rewritten` and as report entries.
- `--migrate-game-paths --dry-run` writes nothing but reports the files a real migration would rewrite (and which rewrite would apply), so a maintainer can preview a migration.
- `--only` and `--migrate-game-paths` are mutually exclusive: `--only` promises "no rewrite", so a run passing both fails fast (exit 1) with an explanatory message rather than half-migrating a repo.
- The exported `rewriteGameTreePaths()` signature is unchanged (other tooling and tests import it directly); only the unconditional call inside `scaffoldGameRepo` is gated.
- Rationale comment in the generator explains why the rewrite became opt-in (the blanket rewrite touched files with no genuine game-tree reference — a drift guard's own `STALE_PREFIX`, run-tests imports, documented local edits).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC3 carried over verbatim — **Path rewrite is opt-in.** `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` and the accompanying quoted-path/alias rewrites run only with `--migrate-game-paths`; without it, no file under `tests/` or `src/` is modified. `--migrate-game-paths` also reports the files it rewrites. _(this slice delivers the opt-in flag and its reporting.)_
- Tests are authored **before** the implementation in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (RED first, then GREEN) for: a default scaffold leaving a temp repo's `tests/**` and `src/**` files byte-identical while `rewritten` is empty; the same tree rewritten with `--migrate-game-paths` and the changed files reported; and a no-genuine-reference file (e.g. a fixture containing the literal `STALE_PREFIX`) staying byte-identical in both modes unless it genuinely contains `example-games/<game>/`.
- `--migrate-game-paths --dry-run` writes nothing and reports the files a real migration would rewrite.
- `--only main.ts --migrate-game-paths` fails fast with a non-zero exit and writes nothing.
- `--help` documents `--migrate-game-paths`, its default-off status and the mutual exclusion with `--only`.
- The targeted unit run (`/skill:test --type unit` scoped to `tests/scripts/`) and `npm run build` pass; the full engine suite passes at the `dev` push gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `migrateGamePaths?: boolean` to `ScaffoldOptions`; replace the unconditional `rewriteGameTreePaths(gameRepoRoot, options.game)` call with `options.migrateGamePaths ? … : []` and a documented rationale comment.
- Extend the classification/report pipeline so a migration run lists the rewritten files (dry-run listed, not written).
- `parseArgs`: `--migrate-game-paths`; reject it together with `--only`; extend `usage()`.
- Tests: extend the temp-repo harness with a `tests/` + `src/` fixture that carries genuine `example-games/<game>/` references and one that carries a decoy (`STALE_PREFIX`, `scripts/run-tests`).

## Prototype/Experiment

None required — the rewrite itself already exists; this slice only changes when it runs.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `migrateGamePaths` option, gated call, dry-run reporting, mutual exclusion, rationale comment.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — rewrite opt-in/no-op/preview tests (authored first).

## Dependencies

- `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` child: _--only allow-list, --force and skip-local write gating_ — selection mode already suppresses rewrites; this slice adds the explicit migration flag and the mutual-exclusion guard.

## Deliverables

An opt-in `--migrate-game-paths` migration with a default-off, no-op-when-absent contract, dry-run preview, mutual exclusion with `--only`, and green targeted unit + build gates.

# Document scaffold write gating in the engine docs

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — the documentation clause of AC5, applied to the engine repository (the consumer-side docs live in the `tce-main-street` follow-up `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`).

## Target outcome

Every engine-repo document that describes the scaffold command documents the new contract: default behaviour for extracted repos is unchanged, `--only` / `--force` gate consumer-owned files, `--dry-run` + `--json` report before writing, and `--migrate-game-paths` is the explicit, opt-in migration.

## Behaviour contract (what the docs must state)

- A **full run** (no `--only`) keeps today's behaviour and is the supported upgrade path for the eight sibling `tce-<game>` repos.
- A **selected run** (`--only <file,...>`) writes only the named generated files; every other file is `skip-local`, and no symlink, asset link or path rewrite is performed.
- `--force` is required to overwrite a selected file whose content differs from the template.
- `--dry-run` writes nothing; `--json` emits the machine-readable per-file classification (`create | update | unchanged | skip-local`) for both dry and real runs.
- `--migrate-game-paths` is opt-in and mutually exclusive with `--only`; fresh repos are already renamed by `extract-repos.sh --path-rename`.
- A worked example of the consumer pattern:
  `tsx core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core --only main.ts --force`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 (per-game repo scaffold) documents the four flags, the unchanged default and the opt-in migration, and its existing example block stays accurate.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (per-game repo scaffold block) and the `README.md` scaffold example document the flags and the consumer pattern; neither still implies that a plain run is always safe in a live checkout.
- Each of `--only`, `--force`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--migrate-game-paths` appears at least once in both `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`.
- No document still claims the scaffold rewrites `tests/` or `src/` unconditionally.
- The generator's header comment links the flag contract to the docs section (a reader of the code finds the prose, and vice versa).
- `npm run build` passes and no documentation-only change breaks the docs/assets checks.

## Minimal Implementation

- Update the §5 scaffold section in `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`: a short "write gating" subsection plus the worked consumer example.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md`'s per-game scaffold block and the `README.md` scaffold example with the flags and the default/opt-in distinction.
- Add the cross-reference comment in the `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` header (the CLI block gains the new flags).

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 scaffold contract.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — per-game repo scaffold block.
- `README.md` — scaffold quick-start example.

Engine documentation that accurately describes default vs. opted-in scaffold behaviour, with a copy-pasteable consumer example and a code↔docs cross-reference.

# `engine-sync.sync --soft`: an interactive dev-start mode that never blocks on a dirty `./core`

## Problem statement

`scripts/engine-sync.mjs` exposes one sync mode whose first act is a hard guard:

```js
if (submoduleIsDirty(repoRoot, coreRel)) {
  throw new EngineSyncError(`engine:sync: ${coreRel} has uncommitted changes — refusing to sync (never clobber). …`);
}
```

That is correct for build paths (`npm run build`, `build:electron`, `implement.py finish`, the dev-push gate) where a dirty submodule must fail loudly. It makes the same function unusable for an **interactive dev start**: a game repo wants `npm run dev` to compose the current engine `dev` tip, but `./core` is routinely dirty while someone works engine-side, so a strict sync would refuse to start the server exactly when the developer needs it.

Operator decision (this session, Q1) is **option B**: add a soft mode rather than wiring the strict `engine:sync` into `dev`.

## Users / user stories

- **Game developer (downstream `tce-<game>` repo):** "As a game developer, `npm run dev` composes the current engine `dev` tip and starts serving, without me running a build or doing submodule surgery first."
- **Engine developer (dirty `./core`):** "As a developer with uncommitted engine edits, `npm run dev` still starts on my working tree, with a loud warning that the engine sync was skipped — my changes are never clobbered or blocked."
- **Release operator (unchanged):** "As a release operator, nothing about `engine:verify` or the strict `engine:sync` build path changes; a dirty submodule still fails a release/build loudly."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `syncEngine({ …, soft: true })` and the CLI `node scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft` exist. With a **dirty** `./core` they perform **no git operation**, log a loud, actionable warning naming the submodule and the reason, and return/exit `0` with `{ updated: false, … , skipped: 'dirty' }` (or equivalent documented field) instead of throwing.
2. Strict mode is **byte-for-byte unchanged**: `sync` without `--soft` (and `syncEngine()` with no `soft` key) still throws the existing `EngineSyncError` message on a dirty submodule, so `npm run build` / `build:electron` / the finish gate keep their current failure semantics (regression-tested).
3. Soft mode changes **only** the dirty-guard outcome. Every other path is identical to strict sync: clean + remote ahead → `git submodule update --remote`, loud `from → to` log, pin rewrite when the repo is pinned, return `updated`; offline/unreachable remote → warn and keep the checkout (already soft); clean + already at tip → no pin write. A dirty-submodule soft run must **not** rewrite the pin or stage the gitlink.
4. `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (`renderPackageJson`) emits the two scripts that let a game repo use soft mode:
   - `dev: "npm run engine:dev-sync && vite --host"`
   - `engine:dev-sync: "node <coreRel>/scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft"`
   and the rendered `package.json` for `main-street` matches the committed `tce-main-street/package.json` for those two entries.
5. `scripts/engine-sync.d.mts` types are updated (`soft?: boolean` on the sync options, the new result field, `SyncResult` doc comment) and `tsc --noEmit` passes for consumers of the declarations.
6. Engine-side tests in `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` cover: (a) dirty submodule + `soft: true` → resolves, no throw, no update, no pin write, warning reported; (b) dirty submodule + strict → still throws the existing message; (c) clean submodule + `soft: true` → same result as strict (update + pin rewrite + staging); (d) CLI `sync --soft` exit code `0` with the warning on stdout/stderr and `sync` exit code `1` on the same fixture; (e) scaffold render assertion for the two scripts (extend the existing render test).
7. CLI usage text documents `--soft` and its dev-start intent; `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (engine) describes the two modes (strict = build/release gate, soft = interactive dev start) wherever `engine:sync` is documented, and the canonical script header comment is updated.
8. All related documentation is updated (engine `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, script docblocks, npm-script comments in the scaffold template).
9. Full project test suite passes; `npm run build` (strict TypeScript + Vite) succeeds.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo ordering:** the engine commit lands on engine `dev` **first**; the downstream gitlink bump + `configs/engine-pin.json` re-pin is tracked in the paired `tce-main-street` item — do not bump from here.
- **No new failure semantics for gates.** Soft mode must be opt-in per call site; no build/release script may use it.
- **Never clobber.** Soft mode's dirty outcome is "skip and warn", never "stash/reset/checkout over" the developer's edits.
- **Scaffold ownership:** the `dev` / `engine:dev-sync` scripts belong in `renderPackageJson`, never hand-edited into a game repo's `package.json`.
- **Do not disturb the dirty engine checkout** at `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` — its main checkout currently has 3 modified `example-games/gym/content/*` files from unrelated work; work in the implement worktree.
- Tests are run through the test skill (`run_tests.py`), never ad hoc.
- UK English in all written output.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/engine-sync.mjs` — `syncEngine({ soft })`, CLI `--soft` flag parsing + usage text, header docblock describing strict vs soft.
- `scripts/engine-sync.d.mts` — `soft?: boolean`, result field, doc comments.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `dev` + `engine:dev-sync` in `renderPackageJson` with an explanatory comment.
- `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` — soft/strict/dirty/clean/CLI cases (fixtures already exist for sync/verify).
- scaffold render test (`grep renderPackageJson` in `tests/scripts/`) — assert the two rendered scripts.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine-sync mode table (strict vs soft) and the "when to use which" rule.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: soft mode masks a stale engine.** Mitigation: the warning is loud and names the reason; strict build paths still catch lag at `engine:verify`/pin. No silent success.
- **Risk: two modes drift.** Mitigation: one code path with a single conditional on the dirty-guard outcome, proven by tests (a) and (c) asserting result equality with strict mode.
- **Risk: game repos start staging pin/gitlink bumps on every `npm run dev`.** Accepted (the pin travels with the gitlink by policy, CG-0MVO268500071BPI) and mitigated by the existing loud `from → to` / pin-log lines; recorded in the paired downstream item.
- **Risk: npm script name proliferation.** Bounded to one wrapper (`engine:dev-sync`) that exists only so `dev` can pass `--soft`; `engine:sync` keeps its meaning.
- **Assumption:** downstream repos invoke the script exactly as scaffolded (`node ./core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs sync --soft`), so no arguments ever reach `dev` from npm.

## Related work

- **CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q** — original engine-sync/verify + scaffold wiring (strict sync in `build`, `verify` in `build:release`); this item adds the opt-in soft mode it did not need then.
- **CG-0MVO268500071BPI** — pin-tracks-tip policy: the pin and the `./core` gitlink always travel together.
- **CG-0MVTVSYQE002JGDN** — git hermeticity contract (`REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`) that soft mode must keep honouring.
- **CG-0MVOCF9T5007CH2A** — local-suite coverage of the pin policy and lag-vs-bad-pin diagnostics (pattern for the new tests).
- **CG-0MVS9HBN3009HIQN** — current in-flight engine item; unrelated, listed to avoid worktree collisions.

## Appendix: decision record

- **Q1 — how should an interactive dev start compose the engine?** Options: (A) strict `npm run engine:sync && vite --host` (dev fails loudly on a dirty submodule); (B) opt-in soft sync mode used by `dev`, strict paths untouched; (C) hand-edit only the game repo's `package.json` (clobbered by re-scaffold). **Answer (operator, this session): B.** Source: producer chat — "Make run dev also run engine:sync" → presented options A/B/C with consequences → "B".
data.title: engine-sync: add a --soft sync mode for interactive dev starts (never block on a dirty ./core)
